scores.reason: Measure type: random (non-fasting) C-peptide. Use is embedded in the ADA/EASD adult type 1 diabetes consensus (and reproduced in ADA Standards 2026 s2 per usecases-verified.md) and in the Jones and Hattersley review; the supporting data are cross-sectional and cohort accuracy studies, with C-peptide mostly serving as the reference standard. No randomized or controlled outcome study of C-peptide-guided treatment change was found in the screened records (one small uncontrolled pilot of 56 patients, 2026, only in Consensus snippet, no PMID checked).

scores.reason: Measure type: random C-peptide. Within its defined subgroup (insulin-treated, more than 3 years from diagnosis, antibody status unclear or negative) C-peptide measures insulin deficiency directly, which clinical features and genetic risk score only approximate (clinical-only models reached AUC 0.95 against histology-defined type 1 diabetes; adding antibodies and genetic risk score gave 0.97, P 0.03; clinical models in youth reached AUC 0.95-0.98 for retained C-peptide). Autoantibodies are the first-line test in the consensus, so C-peptide is second line, not replacing them; scored 3 because no other test measures the treatment-relevant construct, but it is restricted to a subgroup (the 2 versus 3 boundary is a judgement).

scores.reason: Measure type: insulin (with or without C-peptide) and glucose at nadir or during a mixed-meal test. The project sources (review, meta-analysis of CGM prevalence) describe the use and state that no accepted insulin threshold exists; the abstracts screened show case series and small cohorts, with no study testing whether insulin results change management or outcomes. Not found in the screened records: a diagnostic-accuracy study of insulin or C-peptide against a reference standard in post-bariatric patients.

scores.reason: Measure type: insulin and C-peptide at hypoglycaemia. Glucose (Whipple criteria, CGM, mixed-meal glucose nadir) and the timing and surgical history establish the syndrome; insulin and C-peptide add mainly in the defined subgroup where insulinoma, exogenous insulin or sulfonylurea use must be excluded or the picture is atypical. Insulin level itself is not diagnostic in PBH and CGM detects hypoglycaemia more often than symptoms. Low-quality inference from reviews and case reports.

scores.reason: Measure type: fasting-based (HOMA-IR, insulin and glucose). IRIS is a hard-outcome randomized trial (primary outcome HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.62-0.93) but used HOMA-IR above 3.0 only as an entry criterion; it never tested measurement-guided selection or compared patients with and without insulin resistance. Under anchor clarification 8 the maximum is 2. ADA 2026 Rec 3.13 and AACE 2022 R 9.4 repeat the IRIS population without naming an assay or threshold, so they add no independent decision-impact evidence.

scores.reason: Measure type: fasting-based HOMA-IR. No analysis in the screened records tests whether HOMA-IR adds to stroke history plus prediabetes (glucose or HbA1c) for choosing pioglitazone; IRIS enrolled only HOMA-IR above 3.0, so there is no contrast. AACE extends the recommendation to prediabetes or type 2 diabetes with prior stroke, which shows glucose-based criteria are accepted triggers, and the IRIS diabetes-prevention benefit was concentrated in people with impaired fasting glucose or raised HbA1c. Marginal added value is the most the sources support; the HOMA-IR cut-off was chosen as the top quartile of non-diabetic populations (per usecases-verified.md), and insulin is unstandardised.

path_to_viability.missing_piece: Prospective cohort or registry of insulin-treated people reclassified by a standardised random C-peptide threshold, reporting treatment switch, HbA1c, hypoglycaemia and ketoacidosis outcomes against matched non-tested patients, with agreed assay harmonisation.
path_to_viability.basis: Judgement: use is already consensus-backed (D2 3); moving to 4 needs outcome evidence for C-peptide-guided decisions. Only an uncontrolled pilot (n=56) was seen in the screened records; a randomized trial (large) would be ideal but a controlled cohort would raise the tier.

path_to_viability.missing_piece: A diagnostic-accuracy study in post-bariatric patients with symptoms, comparing insulin and C-peptide at documented hypoglycaemia (or mixed-meal nadir) against a reference standard including CGM and clinical course, from which an agreed threshold is derived and then externally validated.
path_to_viability.basis: Judgement: Salehi 2018 (PMID 30101281) and the project note state there is no accepted insulin threshold and no consensus diagnostic criteria; no accuracy study found in the screened records.

path_to_viability.missing_piece: Re-analysis of IRIS (or a pooled pioglitazone dataset) testing HOMA-IR, and non-insulin alternatives such as fasting glucose, HbA1c or triglyceride-to-HDL ratio, as effect modifiers of the pioglitazone benefit on stroke and myocardial infarction, followed by a trial in patients with stroke and prediabetes but low HOMA-IR.
path_to_viability.basis: Judgement: IRIS data are held by the trial team; the pre-specified subgroup analyses showed no heterogeneity but whether HOMA-IR strata were included is not stated in the project notes. A re-analysis uses existing data (small); a new trial would be large.

anchor_issues: Row 6 D8: the anchor 2 (useful in a defined subgroup) versus 3 (clearly adds beyond alternatives) is ambiguous when the whole use is already restricted to a subgroup (insulin-treated, over 3 years). Chose 3 because within that subgroup C-peptide measures the construct directly; a stricter reading gives 2.

Row 6 D2: C-peptide is the reference standard in most accuracy studies, so accuracy data show that other tools predict C-peptide, not that C-peptide changes decisions. Anchor 3 (consensus backed by studies) was applied to the consensus; no anchor covers consensus without outcome studies.

Row 13 D2: anchor clarification 8 (trial entry criterion, maximum 2) overrides the randomized evidence anchor 4; the guidelines cite IRIS, so anchor 3 (guideline backed by studies) was not applied because no study tests measurement-guided selection.

Row 13 D8: IRIS has no comparator without insulin resistance, so 'alternatives do as well' (0) cannot be shown and 'marginal' (1) cannot be proven; chose 1 at low confidence, null would also be defensible.
Row 5 D2 and D8: the row bundles insulin and C-peptide at nadir with mixed-meal testing; evidence for each was not separable.
assumptions: Row 6 uses random C-peptide; stimulated C-peptide (MMTT, glucagon) and urinary C-peptide:creatinine ratio are not scored.
Holt 2021 and ADA Standards 2026 details were taken from the project file (usecases-verified.md, skeptic full-text notes) and not re-read; this unit read abstracts only.
